source: COSMO360 constellation gallery and d3-celestial constellation line data
coordinateNote: Approximate chart centers are calculated from line vertices and are not official IAU boundary centroids.
imageNote: Photographs are COSMO360-hosted 960 px WebP derivatives. Attribution, source, and CC BY 4.0 license are recorded for each.

constellations.name: Andromeda
constellations.description: A chain of stars leads to the light of another galaxy. Nearby landmarks share a patch of sky with an object whose light has traveled for millions of years.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Antlia
constellations.description: The air pump of Antlia recalls the scientific instruments that inspired several constellations in the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Apus
constellations.description: Apus, the Bird of Paradise, is an exotic figure deep in the southern sky. Its pattern is made up of relatively faint stars.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Aquarius
constellations.description: The extended figure of Aquarius contains the glowing shell of a dying star. Its color portrait tells a story of gas and ultraviolet light.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Aquila
constellations.description: Aquila stands out around Altair, one of the Summer Triangle's three corners. Under dark skies the familiar pattern appears against the Milky Way, where bright stars alternate with dark dust lanes.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Ara
constellations.description: Ara is an altar in the southern sky. Its star pattern lies south of Scorpius.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Aries
constellations.description: Aries is the celestial ram. A short chain of its main stars lies between Pisces and Taurus.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Auriga
constellations.description: Auriga depicts a celestial charioteer. Its broad pattern stands out around bright Capella.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Boötes
constellations.description: Boötes is the herdsman of the northern sky. Its stars form an elongated figure with Arcturus shining at its base.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Caelum
constellations.description: Caelum represents an engraver's chisel. This compact southern figure shows that not all constellations are linked to myths.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Camelopardalis
constellations.description: Camelopardalis, the Giraffe, covers a large area of the northern sky. Its faint stars fill the space between brighter neighboring figures.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Cancer
constellations.description: Cancer is a small figure on the ecliptic. Its stars are noticeably fainter than the bright stars of neighboring Gemini and Leo.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Canes Venatici
constellations.description: Canes Venatici represents a pair of hunting dogs. Its small pattern lies beneath the arc of Ursa Major.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Canis Major
constellations.description: The brightest star in the night sky shares a direction with a distant bubble of gas. Canis Major offers a striking illustration of the depth of space.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Canis Minor
constellations.description: Canis Minor is recognizable by a short line beside Procyon. Its minimal pattern neatly illustrates the imagined nature of constellation figures.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Capricornus
constellations.description: Capricornus is the mythical sea goat. Its broad, angular figure lies on the ecliptic.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Carina
constellations.description: The keel of an ancient celestial ship leads to a region where massive stars are born. An infrared camera reveals what dust conceals.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Cassiopeia
constellations.description: Five main points form a celestial letter. But leave a camera's shutter open, and the familiar figure becomes arcs of time.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zaman CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Centaurus
constellations.description: One of the Sun's nearest neighbors shines in the rich southern sky. But proximity on a map does not make all of Centaurus's stars close to us.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Cepheus
constellations.description: Cepheus is a celestial king. Its main lines resemble a little house in the northern sky beside Cassiopeia.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Cetus
constellations.description: Cetus depicts a sea monster. This large figure south of Pisces and Aries extends across both sides of the celestial equator.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Chamaeleon
constellations.description: Chamaeleon is a small figure near the south celestial pole. Its stars are easier to see from southern latitudes.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Circinus
constellations.description: Circinus represents a drawing compass. Its narrow southern figure lies beside Centaurus.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Columba
constellations.description: Columba is a small dove south of Lepus. A few main stars form its compact silhouette.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zaman CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Coma Berenices
constellations.description: Coma Berenices is named after a queen's hair. Its faint pattern lies north of Virgo.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Corona Australis
constellations.description: Corona Australis is a small crown beneath Sagittarius. The arc of its main stars explains its name.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Corona Borealis
constellations.description: Corona Borealis is a semicircular crown between Boötes and Hercules. Its curved shape is especially clear on a star map.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Corvus
constellations.description: Corvus forms a compact quadrilateral south of Virgo. The corners of the figure make useful guideposts for finding it.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Crater
constellations.description: Crater is a cup resting on the long celestial Hydra. Its pattern consists of relatively faint stars.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Crux
constellations.description: The smallest official constellation left a large mark on the history of navigation. Four bright points stand out against the rich southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Cygnus
constellations.description: Outstretched wings above the Milky Way. In Cygnus, a simple pattern crosses a complex landscape of stars, gas and dark dust.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Delphinus
constellations.description: Delphinus is a compact diamond with a short tail. This little figure lies beside Aquila.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Dorado
constellations.description: Dorado, the Dolphinfish, is a southern constellation. Its elongated pattern lies beside Reticulum and Pictor.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Draco
constellations.description: Draco winds through the northern constellations in a long chain of stars. Its region contains Thuban, a guide to celestial north long before today's Pole Star.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Equuleus
constellations.description: Equuleus, the Little Horse, is a small figure beside Pegasus. Its faint stars require darker skies.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Eridanus
constellations.description: Eridanus is a celestial river. Its long chain of stars flows from the region around Orion deep into the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Fornax
constellations.description: Fornax represents a scientific furnace. Its small pattern lies among faint stars in the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Gemini
constellations.description: Two bright stars mark the celestial Twins' heads. Behind these similar points lie different systems: Pollux is a nearby giant, while Castor contains several stars.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Grus
constellations.description: Grus is a large crane in the southern sky. Its main lines suggest a long neck and outstretched wings.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Hercules
constellations.description: Hercules is the hero of Greek mythology. At the center of its large figure is a quadrilateral known as the Keystone.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Horologium
constellations.description: Horologium represents a timekeeping instrument. Its long, faint figure lies in the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Hydra
constellations.description: Hydra is a long celestial water snake. Its chain of stars stretches across a large area of the sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Hydrus
constellations.description: Hydrus, the Lesser Water Snake, is a separate figure near the south celestial pole. It should not be confused with the much larger equatorial Hydra.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Indus
constellations.description: Indus is a human figure in the southern sky. Its pattern lies between Grus and Pavo.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Lacerta
constellations.description: Lacerta, the Lizard, is a small zigzag of northern stars. It fills the space between Cygnus, Cassiopeia and Pegasus.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Leo
constellations.description: Regulus marks the base of the celestial Sickle, a pattern resembling a backward question mark. Faraway galaxies lie apart from the bright stars.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Leo Minor
constellations.description: Leo Minor is a separate, faint figure between Leo and Ursa Major. Its name connects these neighboring regions of the sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Lepus
constellations.description: Lepus, the Hare, hides beneath Orion's feet. Its compact pattern lies south of bright Rigel.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Libra
constellations.description: Libra depicts a pair of scales. It is one of the constellations on the ecliptic, between Virgo and Scorpius.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Lupus
constellations.description: Lupus, the Wolf, is a southern figure beside Centaurus. Several prominent stars form its elongated pattern.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Lynx
constellations.description: Lynx consists of a long chain of faint stars. Its name recalls the keen eyesight needed to observe it.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Lyra
constellations.description: Bright Vega makes little Lyra noticeable even before its fainter stars emerge. Beyond a simple parallelogram lie a multiple system and the shell of a star that has finished its ordinary life.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Mensa
constellations.description: Mensa brings an earthly mountain, Table Mountain, into the southern sky. Its very faint stars lie near the south celestial pole.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Microscopium
constellations.description: Microscopium represents a scientific instrument. Its faint rectangular figure lies in the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Monoceros
constellations.description: Monoceros, the Unicorn, is a mythical animal between the bright figures of Orion and the Dogs. Its own stars are much fainter than those of its neighbors.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Musca
constellations.description: Musca, the Fly, is a small figure south of the Southern Cross. Its compact pattern is easier to observe from southern latitudes.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Norma
constellations.description: Norma represents a draftsman's square. Its faint stars form a small southern pattern.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Octans
constellations.description: Octans represents an instrument for measuring angles. It contains the south celestial pole, which has no equivalent of bright Polaris.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Ophiuchus
constellations.description: Near Scorpius, bright clouds meet almost black dust. In Ophiuchus, an apparently empty part of a photograph is often the most revealing.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Orion
constellations.description: Three stars in a row are only the beginning. Beyond Orion's familiar Belt lies a vast region where stars are born inside clouds of gas and dust.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Pavo
constellations.description: Pavo, the Peacock, is a bird of the southern sky. Its chains of stars fan out around the main guide stars.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Pegasus
constellations.description: The Great Square of Pegasus helps you navigate the autumn sky. From its four prominent corners, explore Andromeda, an ancient star cluster and the star that began a new era in the search for exoplanets.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Perseus
constellations.description: Two stellar islands side by side in the sky. In Perseus, compare a constellation's pattern with real groups of young stars.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Phoenix
constellations.description: Phoenix is the legendary bird of rebirth. Its stars form a compact pattern in the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Pictor
constellations.description: Pictor represents a painter's equipment. Its elongated, faint figure lies beside Carina.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Pisces
constellations.description: Pisces depicts two fish joined by a ribbon. Its large but faint pattern crosses the ecliptic.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Piscis Austrinus
constellations.description: Piscis Austrinus, the Southern Fish, is a separate figure beneath Aquarius. Fomalhaut is its bright guide star.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Puppis
constellations.description: Puppis represents the stern of a celestial ship. It is a separate region of the southern sky beside Vela and Carina.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Pyxis
constellations.description: Pyxis, the Compass, recalls marine navigation. Its small figure lies in the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Reticulum
constellations.description: Reticulum represents the crosshairs in an astronomical instrument. A small diamond of main stars lies far to the south.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Sagitta
constellations.description: Sagitta, the Arrow, is a tiny figure of just a few stars. Its point and shaft are easy to trace on a map between Aquila and Vulpecula.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Sagittarius
constellations.description: The Milky Way's light rises above the spout of the celestial Teapot. This direction leads toward one of our Galaxy's richest stellar landscapes.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Scorpius
constellations.description: Red Antares sets the character of the entire figure. Around it, the sky becomes layered: bright stars, nebulae and dust overlap one another.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Sculptor
constellations.description: Sculptor represents an artist's work. Its faint pattern lies in the southern sky beside Phoenix and Cetus.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Scutum
constellations.description: Scutum is a small celestial shield. Its faint stars lie between Aquila and Sagittarius.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Serpens
constellations.description: Ophiuchus divides Serpens into a head and a tail. Despite occupying two separate regions, it is one of the 88 constellations.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Sextans
constellations.description: Sextans represents a measuring instrument. Its faint figure lies south of Leo.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Taurus
constellations.description: A bright orange eye and a scattering of blue stars. Taurus combines an easy celestial landmark with one of the most striking star clusters.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Telescopium
constellations.description: Telescopium represents the instrument that revealed worlds invisible to the naked eye. Its compact figure lies deep in the southern sky.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Triangulum
constellations.description: Triangulum is a simple figure of three main stars. This small northern pattern lies beside Andromeda.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Triangulum Australe
constellations.description: Triangulum Australe, the Southern Triangle, is a separate figure in the southern sky. Three prominent stars form its recognizable corners.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Tucana
constellations.description: Tucana, the Toucan, is a bird of the far southern sky. Its lines connect several relatively faint stars.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Ursa Major
constellations.description: The Big Dipper helps you navigate the northern sky. But its seven familiar stars are only part of Ursa Major: the official region is much larger.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Ursa Minor
constellations.description: Polaris marks the end of the Little Dipper's handle. It helps you find north, but the other stars in the pattern require darker skies.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zaman CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Vela
constellations.description: Vela represents the sails of a celestial ship. Its large southern pattern lies beside Puppis and Carina.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Virgo
constellations.description: Spica marks the way to Virgo in the spring sky. Its bright stars belong to the Milky Way, while in the same direction lie galaxies whose light takes tens of millions of years to reach us.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Volans
constellations.description: Volans is a southern figure representing a flying fish. Its stars lie beside Carina.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0

constellations.name: Vulpecula
constellations.description: Vulpecula, the Little Fox, is a small, faint figure beneath Cygnus. It fills the patch of sky between Sagitta and its brighter neighbors.
constellations.credit: Photo: E. Slawik/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/M. Zamani CC BY 4.0
